methodological_rigor.justification: The study combines IFNγ-mediated phenotype remodeling on a newly characterized UPS cell line (JBT19), IC50 determination by MTT for docetaxel/doxorubicin/mitomycin C, cell cycle/PI staining with Dean/Jett/Fox modeling, Annexin V apoptosis assay, flow cytometry with fluorescence-minus-one gating, and generation of JBT19-reactive lymphocytes from buffy coats of four donors with rapid expansion protocol and GFP-based cytotoxicity readouts. The experimental design is layered and orthogonal (time-course, reversibility, MHC blocking, different chemotherapeutics). Limitations: single tumor cell line, no in vivo validation, modest donor numbers (n=4) for lymphocyte experiments, and analyses rely on unpaired/paired t-tests and one-way ANOVA without explicit multiplicity control across many phenotypic markers.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: A mechanistic in vitro study on a single UPS-derived cell line with allogeneic PBMC-derived lymphocytes, mapping to Oxford LoE 5. The observation that IFNγ induces docetaxel resistance (>2,000-fold IC50 shift) while simultaneously enabling adaptive immune killing is translationally interesting and speaks to sequencing of chemotherapy and immunotherapy, but no patient tissue, organoid, or in vivo model is included.

reporting_quality.justification: No animals are used; reporting standards for cell-based studies are not formal (ARRIVE only partially applicable, and not referenced). Methods are thorough: clones, catalog numbers, fluorophores, reagent vendors, antibody blocking conditions, cell seeding densities, and ethics approval (EK-602.4/22) are explicitly stated. Statistical analyses are described but multiplicity control is not detailed. No data or flow cytometry .fcs repository deposition is mentioned; JBT19 cell line provenance is cited (ref 28).

novelty_literature.justification: The central finding, that IFNγ simultaneously induces docetaxel resistance while the same cells remain susceptible to cytotoxic lymphocytes, addresses a clinically important but poorly studied interaction between immunotherapy-driven IFNγ and subsequent chemotherapy efficacy, specifically in UPS. The paper introduces novel data on the recently established JBT19 line and documents reversibility of IFNγ-induced changes over ~24 days. Prior work has documented IFNγ-driven PD-L1/MHC effects, but the integrated dual-role framing here is genuinely novel.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear narrative arc: IFNγ induces phenotypic remodeling and chemoresistance, is reversible after ~24 days of washout, yet reactive lymphocytes still kill the remodeled cells. Figures 1-4+ are described in detail with time-course, concentration-response, cell-cycle, Ki-67, PD-L1/MHC-I/MHC-II panels, and reversibility experiments. Prose is occasionally dense but technically precise; controls and rationale for each step are explained.

key_strengths: Novel dual-role finding: IFNγ induces >2,000-fold docetaxel resistance while permitting effective lymphocyte-mediated killing of the remodeled UPS cells
Reversibility experiments (24-day washout) convincingly establish that IFNγ-induced changes are transient rather than permanent
Orthogonal phenotypic readouts (Ki-67, PD-L1, MHC-I/II, CD44/47/95, STAT1, MDR-1, Bcl-2) paint a coherent picture of remodeling
Ethics-approved use of PBMCs from four healthy donors with rapid expansion protocol and GFP-based cytotoxicity assay
key_concerns: Single tumor cell line (JBT19) and single epithelial comparator (PC-3); generalizability to other UPS or sarcoma tumors unproven
No in vivo validation (xenograft or syngeneic model) to confirm that IFNγ-induced chemoresistance and immune-mediated killing coexist in a tumor microenvironment
Multiplicity control not explicitly addressed across many phenotypic markers and comparisons
No deposition of raw flow cytometry or image data; data-availability statement not visible
Chemotherapy breadth limited: docetaxel is the main focus; doxorubicin and mitomycin C results not extensively shown
chief_reviewer.rationale: A carefully executed mechanistic in vitro study presenting a clinically relevant and novel dual-role observation for IFNγ in UPS; suitable for Tier 3 after minor revisions to add multiplicity control discussion and ideally in vivo confirmation.
